subject.title: Cross-provider fallback should respect provider trust boundaries for images/attachments

question: Should configured cross-provider model fallback imply consent to transfer user media, or should OpenClaw add a separate provider media trust policy for fallback retries?
rationale: The source shows a real sensitive-data boundary, but the permanent default affects compatibility, fallback usefulness, and disclosure expectations.

options.title: Add explicit media trust policy
options.body: Preserve current behavior by default if maintainers choose compatibility, but add config, docs, and runtime checks so users can restrict images and attachments on cross-provider fallback.

options.title: Document fallback as full consent
options.body: Keep forwarding semantics and make the docs state that configured cross-provider fallbacks may receive prompt text, images, and attachments.

options.title: Fail closed for cross-provider media
options.body: Strip cross-provider media by default and require explicit opt-in when users want vision-capable fallback behavior across providers.

recommendation.title: Add explicit media trust policy
recommendation.body: Preserve current behavior by default if maintainers choose compatibility, but add config, docs, and runtime checks so users can restrict images and attachments on cross-provider fallback.
